answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network enforces quadratic cryptographic stake burning for identity registration. Minting n identities requires burning stake scaling as O(n^2), elevating attacker costs to an impossible zenith where running duplicate bots exhausts capital exponentially faster than any marginal payoff. Under this protocol, identity validation acts like a bright lantern exposing cluster origins, so malicious spoofing attempts scatter like a weak zephyr against immovable economic friction.
